answer: To join the market, each agent must lock a refundable stake — a marble placed in escrow that only returns if the agent behaves. A Sybil attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand stakes, so the cost of flooding the network rises with every sockpuppet, and an umber ledger records each forfeiture. Reputation then acts as a bridge between past behavior and future trust: honest agents accumulate standing, while fresh fakes start at zero and cannot buy history. Misbehavior triggers slashing that burns the stake, so attacks cost real money.
